title: Japanese Corn Gyoza
description: A traditional Tohoku dish featuring cornmeal and tempering chocolate, served in a molcajete vessel, this satvik-friendly recipe is a nostalgic treat for the senses, with a bouncy-qq texture that is both cultured and delightful.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine cornmeal and all purpose flour.
Gradually add water to the bowl, stirring with a wooden spoon until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces and roll each piece into a ball.
Flatten each ball into a disk shape using a rolling pin.
Place a tablespoon of melted tempering chocolate in the center of each disk.
Fold the disk in half to form a half moon shape and press the edges together to seal the gyoza.
Heat sesame oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the gyoza for 2-3 minutes on each side.
Serve the gyoza in a molcajete vessel garnished with chopped green onions.
